articles.title: Jammu Kashmir Govt Directs Departments to Clear Electricity Dues on Time - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: The Jammu and Kashmir Government has directed all government departments to ensure timely payment of electricity bills, warning that delays have resulted in substantial outstanding arrears, additional financial liabilities through late payment surcharges and penalties, and an avoidable burden on the public exchequer.
In a circular issued on November 16, 2026, the Finance Department asked all departments to establish an effective mechanism for prompt settlement of electricity dues and ensure strict compliance with the instructions through their respective Directors Finance and Financial Advisors.
The department said delayed payments were also affecting the financial stability of power utilities, which is essential for maintaining reliable electricity supply and reducing the gap between the Average Cost of Supply (ACS) and Aggregate Revenue Receipts (ARR).
It further pointed out that the pre-qualification criteria under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) mandate 100 per cent payment of current electricity dues by all government departments, local bodies and autonomous bodies for the year under evaluation.
The circular, issued by the Director General (Budget), Finance Department, also provides for departments facing a shortage of funds to arrange the required amount through re-appropriation.
It directs departments to first reconcile their outstanding electricity dues with the Jammu and Kashmir Power Development Department (JKPDD). If a shortage of funds is identified under the relevant Head of Account after reconciliation, the concerned departments have been asked to identify savings under other appropriate Detailed Heads or Heads within the funds released for the current financial year.
They have also been directed to process cases for re-appropriation in accordance with the prescribed procedure.
Rs 763.91 crore released for electricity charges
The annexure accompanying the circular provides department-wise details of budget estimates, funds released and expenditure under Detailed Head 008 (Electricity Charges) for the financial year 2026-27.
According to the figures, the Finance Department has released Rs 763.91 crore against an equal budgetary provision of Rs 763.91 crore for electricity charges across 35 departments. The reported expenditure so far stands at Rs 495.88 crore.
The Health and Medical Education Department accounts for the highest allocation, with Rs 148.87 crore released against an equal budget estimate. Its expenditure has been recorded at Rs 75.02 crore.
The Public Health Engineering Department under Jal Shakti has received Rs 457.21 crore, against which expenditure stands at Rs 348.00 crore.
The Irrigation and Flood Control Department under Jal Shakti has been allocated Rs 49.81 crore, with expenditure of Rs 30.53 crore.
The Housing and Urban Development Department has received Rs 15.69 crore and recorded expenditure of Rs 9.71 crore, while the Hospitality and Protocol Department has been allocated Rs 17.83 crore, against which expenditure stands at Rs 3.51 crore.
The Education Department has received Rs 8.54 crore, with expenditure of Rs 3.85 crore, while the Agriculture Production Department has been allocated Rs 6.61 crore and recorded expenditure of Rs 2.72 crore.
The Finance Department has received Rs 3.50 crore, against which expenditure stands at Rs 1.07 crore.
